§9The Universe§r, one at a time inside the crown. Each universe lives one§9 7,200 s batch§r, from first light to last. The job is cosmology's oldest problem: §9keep it flat§r. Too much matter and it recollapses (a Big Crunch); too little and dark energy tears it apart (a Big Rip).

§5§lTHE §lFIELD§r Gauges P and §9H§r, the expansion error against the Friedmann curve the crown follows. H drifts up as dark energy takes over late in each universe (runaway gain +0.01). Trims: §9Attractor Dark Matter§r 4 L = H −2 (more mass, gravity slows it); §9Molten SpaceTime§r 100 L = H +2; Spatially Enlarged Fluid 100 L = P −2. Caps 10 a second. W, Λ, V and the beam retire. Demand§9 96 Bu/t§r (9.6e14 EU/t) on the crown's 12 ports.

§5§lEVENTS§r §9Recombination§r at 1,800 s (warned 60 s): the universe turns transparent, H climbs for 300 s. §9Cosmic Dawn§r once a universe at 3,240 to 4,680 s (warned 120 s): the first stars ignite across the crown. Held Stable throughout: +12.5 % Universium.

§5§lOUTPUT§r §9Universium 9,216 L a universe§r × mean Y × r, + 1,152 L for a caught Cosmic Dawn: about 6,200 L an hour. The charge is 9,216 L Attractor Dark Matter a universe. This is the §9only§r Universium source. A Big Rip or Crunch ends that universe early and salvages 25 % × the fraction run; the Eye never loses T10. If the universe goes out (the structure broken, the Eye switched off), the dark Eye begins a §9new universe§r at T10 from a new 9,216 L charge.

§5§lALL §lIT §lHOLDS§r Each finished universe also yields its stars and planets (× p × mean Y × r): Excited Stellar Plasma 300,000 L, Raw Hyperdense Stellar Plasma 75,000 L, White Dwarf Matter 18,420 L, Black Dwarf Matter 4,608 L, Magnetar Matter 1,800 L, Ergomatter 72,000 L, Superdense Ergomatter 36,000 L, and §9every planet once§r at parallel 2^(10 - k), each parallel at (1 - 0.05 R) × the batch's field factor (no H/He, no EU; items to the ME output bus). Raw Star Matter comes every Eye-minute: 500,000 L × p × Y × r. A collapsed universe yields none of it.
- §9The filter§r: the slot bus is a whitelist, never used up. Planet items keep only those planets; star charts of T2 to T8 keep only their matters; empty, everything comes. An ME interface or export bus can set it.
- Two toggles on the Galaxy panel switch the star matter and the planets off (OpenComputers setUniverseYield(stars, planets); redstone: a Directive Hatch on its yield control set, bit 1 star matter, bit 2 planets, 4 both off). The Yield row shows what the next universe gives.

§5§lSTANDARD §lRIG§r Universe bits 1 and 2 to two 2-unit valves (Dark Matter and SpaceTime), J1 on P, the Space valve, and a 600 SM quasar.

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r you have 144 L of Universium.
